Billie Jean King. An American tennis pioneer who won twelve Grand Slam singles titles and became a global icon for gender equality through her landmark "Battle of the Sexes" match in 1973. Her advocacy for equal pay and women's rights transcended tennis itself, making her one of sports's most influential and transformative figures. She won twelve Grand Slam singles titles: one Australian Open, one French Open, six Wimbledons, and four US Opens, demonstrating consistency and excellence across multiple major tournaments. She also won thirty-nine Grand Slam titles across singles, doubles, and mixed doubles, including a record six Wimbledon doubles titles that stood as a benchmark of excellence. Most famously, in 1973 she defeated the fifty-five-year-old Bobby Riggs in an exhibition match played in straight sets. This became a watershed moment for women's sports and gender equality, capturing the imagination of millions. She reached world number one in 1966 and dominated the 1960s and 1970s, establishing herself as one of the era's greatest players. Her six Wimbledon singles titles showcase her grass-court mastery and competitive excellence. She co-founded the Women's Tennis Association and fought tirelessly throughout her career for equal prize money and tournament opportunities for women. She won twenty consecutive matches at Wimbledon between 1966 and 1968, and appeared in twenty major finals, establishing herself as one of tennis's all-time greats.
